newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian CPI to help hold down rates - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australian CPI to help hold down rates - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the March quarter inflation data would help maintain a low interest rate environment and that there was every reason to expect low inflation to continue.
Government inflation forecasts for the current fiscal year, to June 30, 1997, and for 1997/98 were well on track and low inflation expectations would also help entrench low inflation, he said.
Costello said: "The March quarter CPI (consumer price index) outcome continues the very good inflation performance of the past year and there is every reason for believing this will continue."
"The outcome is consistent with the Reserve Bank's inflation objective and as such will contribute to the maintenance of a low-interest-rate environment."
The government was still finalising the economic forecasts it would issue in the May 13 budget but the latest forecasts, issued in January, were looking good, he said.
"... It is clear that the mid-year economic and fiscal outlook forecasts for continued very low inflation in 1996/97 and 1997/98 remain well on track," he said.
"The step down in consumer inflationary expectations over the past 12 months will help entrench low inflation."
The government forecasts that average consumer prices for 1996/97 will be 1.5 percent higher than in 1995/96.
On the same "year-average" basis, inflation will be 1.75 percent in 1997/98, the government forecasts.
Underlying prices, which exclude some volatile items, are forecast to rise 2.0 percent between the June quarters of 1995 and 1996.
Earlier on Wednesday, the official statistician said overall consumer prices rose 1.3 percent between the March quarters of 1995 and 1996, while underlying prices rose 2.1 percent,
"The continuation of a very low rate of underlying inflation is a result of ongoing competitive pressures in the economy combined with the appreciation of the dollar since mid-1995," Costello said.
The Reserve Bank says it conducts monetary policy with the aim of keeping the annual rate of underlying inflation at an average between two and three percent.
The bank eased monetary policy three times between July and December 1996, each time lowering its overnight cash rate target by 0.5 percentage points. Cash rates are currently 6.0 percent.
